q: What is the carbon footprint of a smartphone per handset?
title: Smartphone footprint per handset
short: Most of a phone's footprint comes from making it, mainly the chips and the display, not from charging it. Use the brand's published product report for that model if one exists. A company buying phones for staff counts them in Scope 3, usually Category 2 if they are capitalised.
audience: Companies buying phones for staff, and phone assemblers

ul: Manufacturing: integrated circuits, display, battery and casing.
Use: charging electricity, a small share over the phone's life.
End of life: collection and recycling.

p: Count each phone once, in the year you buy it, using the model's published figure. If none exists, use a spend-based factor and label it as an estimate.

senseible: Senseible reads the energy invoices behind the making stage into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, and keeps material invoices on the Scope 3 trail. Material factors come from your supplier or a named database and are labelled with their source, so the product figure can be traced line by line.
